paragraphs: Friend, here's what the whole book of Ecclesiastes comes down to. After all the searching and pondering, the Teacher's last word is not a puzzle. "When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man." (Ecclesiastes 12:13) Whole duty, baker. No fine print, no secret extra page, and I know fine print.

So why does that matter to you on a regular Tuesday? Because the passage says the words of the wise are "like goads" and "like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd." (Ecclesiastes 12:11) Good words aren't just there to decorate your brain. They poke you forward, and they hold you steady. And the passage also warns that "There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body," (Ecclesiastes 12:12) so don't wear yourself out chasing every new idea when the Shepherd has already handed you the nails.

The last line gives the reason, and it's one to take to heart. "For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil." (Ecclesiastes 12:14) That means your quiet, unseen choices matter, even the ones nobody clapped for. So take it from a stamper who got pulled out of a dark drawer: fear God, keep His commandments, and keep your ovens ready.
